evidence: BroadcastRadius busts the cached business row (bustBusinessGetCache) and invalidates the query cache after saving, so going back doesn't show the old radius.

No map visualiser: the screen explains in words what the radius covers (bookings, community posts and stories — not Explore or Search) and shows the value in km. Drawing the circle over the shop's location is a v1.1 improvement, not a defect. Deferred to v1.1 under decision D17 (owner to confirm).
Both surfaces write the same businesses.broadcast_radius through businessService.update, and the profile editor seeds from the saved value, so they can't disagree.

A live 'this many neighbours' estimate would need a count of users inside the radius, which is exactly the kind of population query the privacy model keeps off the client. Deferred as a product question rather than fixed with a guess. Deferred to v1.1 under decision D17 (owner to confirm).

_bulk_deal_close_internal handles a campaign with no deposit (staging source check, 2026-09-16) and E2E critical/bulk-deal drives a deposit campaign end to end (E2E-039 fixed the close path in 20260979).
bulk_deal_delete guards with raise exception and accounts for issued tokens (production source check), so deleting can't quietly void customers' claim passes.
bulk_deal_close, bulk_deal_extend and bulk_deal_delete all consult has_business_scope, so a delegated manager can run a campaign.
The redemption panel shows 'Balance to collect' from the token's balanceDue whenever one remains (BulkDealsManager).
bulk_deal_token_redeem checks the token's business_id, so a pass from another shop can't be accepted (production source check).
The deal console surfaces the server's message (e?.message) on confirm, reject, close and extend instead of a blanket failure.
grep '#fff' in the bulk-deal console and card: none (2026-09-16); the composer is part of BulkDealsManager, which uses tokens.

The manager reads businessService.portfolioItems (the shop's own rows) instead of the enriched public list, so curated stand-ins for an empty portfolio no longer appear as items the owner can caption or delete.
Edit and delete are 40px targets, and delete opens a confirmation sheet showing the photo before removing it.
updatePortfolio and deletePortfolio select the affected rows and throw when nothing was touched, so a write RLS refuses is reported instead of looking like success.
All three portfolio writes bust the cached business row, and the manager's own query refetches, so an upload, caption or deletion shows immediately here and on the public page.

uploadService throws UPLOAD_FAILED instead of falling back to a base64 data URL (E2E-015); nothing writes an image into a text column any more. Migrating rows written before that fix is an owner step.
The caption editor has a cancel button that restores the previous caption and closes the editor.

Ordering and a hero pick need a sort column on business_portfolio_items plus drag-and-drop; the table has no ordering field (id, business_id, url, caption, created_at) and the gallery shows newest first. A v1.1 feature. Deferred to v1.1 under decision D17 (owner to confirm).
grep '#fff' in BusinessPortfolio.tsx: none (2026-09-16), and every control is at least 40px with an aria-label.
businessService.update busts the cached business row, so the profile hub and the verification panel read the same status after a submission.
The profile hub reads verificationStatus: 'Under review' while UNDER_REVIEW, 'Verification declined — try again' when REJECTED, instead of inviting the owner to 'Get verified' again.
A PDF over 5 MB is refused when picked, with the file named, rather than failing later inside storage; images go through the compressor.

Submitted documents are KYC material: the panel deliberately doesn't re-display them, and withdrawing a review would need an admin-side state change. Worth revisiting with the verification queue in v1.1; the owner can see the status and resubmit after a decision. Deferred to v1.1 under decision D17 (owner to confirm).
The status cards use theme tokens (var(--green-*), var(--amber-*), var(--red-*)) — no colour literals in VerificationPanel.tsx.
The item editor sends explicit nulls (salePrice: sale.trim() ? Number(sale) : null, image: image ? image : null), so clearing a sale price or photo persists instead of being dropped as undefined.
Deleting a catalog item opens a confirmation sheet naming the item (confirmDelete state in CatalogManager).

Manual ordering needs a sort column and a drag handle; the list is grouped and stable per fetch today. A v1.1 improvement for shops with long catalogs. Deferred to v1.1 under decision D17 (owner to confirm).
Any item can be marked unavailable and back ('Marked as unavailable' / 'Marked as available'), and a finite item that hits zero flips to OUT_OF_STOCK automatically.
The shop page's cart stepper caps a FINITE item at the quantity left, so a customer can't order more than the shop has.

Catalog search and category grouping matter at a size no v1 shop has yet (the editor lists items with their photos and prices). A v1.1 improvement. Deferred to v1.1 under decision D17 (owner to confirm).
The catalog console subscribes to catalog_items (or provider_packages) for this entity and refetches, so a change made on another device lands without a manual refresh.
The file input is reset after each pick (e.target.value = ""), so the same photo can be chosen twice in a row; the editor's surfaces use theme tokens.
Every stock write busts the cached business row and invalidates business:<id>, then refetches, so the inventory screen, the catalog console and the public page agree.
The stepper stays usable on an out-of-stock item: +1 sets quantity 1 and IN_STOCK, and reaching zero sets OUT_OF_STOCK, so restocking never needs a detour through the item editor.
InventoryAlerts renders ManageNav for businesses, so the merchant can leave the screen.

Migration 20260985 adds catalog_item_adjust_quantity (row-locked delta, keeps stock_status consistent, checks the caller manages the catalog) and the console uses it, so two people restocking at once add up instead of overwriting each other. Forced-rollback tested on staging: before, the function didn't exist (42883); after, 5 → +3 → −10 lands at 0 / OUT_OF_STOCK and a stranger gets NOT_CATALOG_MANAGER.

The low-stock line is a fixed 5 (LOW_STOCK_THRESHOLD). A per-item threshold needs a column and an editor field; the fixed value is honest about what it means today. A v1.1 improvement. Deferred to v1.1 under decision D17 (owner to confirm).

The screen already splits items into Out of stock / Running low / healthy, which is the filter that matters at v1 catalog sizes. Search is a v1.1 improvement. Deferred to v1.1 under decision D17 (owner to confirm).
businessService.update busts the cached business row, so a saved profile shows everywhere instead of the app serving the old copy.
uploadService throws instead of storing a base64 data URL when storage refuses (E2E-015), so a failed cover upload can't bloat the row.

Deliberate: /business/:id/manage/profile sits under RequireOwner with the comment 'Owner-only — FULL delegates and scoped team members are bounced'. Branding, category and contact details are the owner's to change; team members manage the day-to-day surfaces.

A location move is review-gated through requestLocationChange (pending_lat/pending_lng) and the admin decision writes back status and rejection_reason, which the console surfaces; businessService.update strips lat/lng so nothing can move the pin silently.
The category picker resolves the parent from children (parentCat) and saves categoryId plus categoryName, so choosing a subcategory persists as that subcategory.
Saving refuses an invalid phone, WhatsApp number or pincode with a specific message ('Enter a valid 10-digit mobile number', 'A pincode is 6 digits'), instead of saving a shop nobody can reach.
grep '#fff' in ProfileEditor.tsx: none (2026-09-16).
answerQuestion selects the updated row and throws when nothing was written, so an answer RLS refuses no longer shows 'Answer posted'.
QnaManager renders ManageNav, so answering a question is no longer a dead end.
Posting an answer refetches the list (onChanged), so the card moves into the answered group in the same sort order the screen defines.

Each question has a 'Report this question' action (ReportSheet, target type QUESTION) so spam reaches the admin queue; admins act on it there, and AdminPanel says so rather than filing it as handled (MOD-2).
Editing an answer has a Cancel that restores the posted text and leaves edit mode.
The answer box is capped at 1000 characters and the answer is saved trimmed.
The manual override is visible as its own state ('Manual override' badge, 'Manual override is active') with a way back to the schedule, so a shop can't be stuck manually closed without knowing why.
getDayWindows handles overnight windows (to < from) and the previous day's spill past midnight (src/utils/availability.ts), and the unit tests cover it.
calculateNextTurnoffTime returns today's closing time when it is still ahead and only then moves to the next day's close, instead of always leaping 24 hours forward; covered by availability.test.ts.
Toggling open/closed saves pending hour edits first (isDirty && hoursRaw !== undefined → businessService.update), with the comment recording the claim (HRS-4).

Hours are evaluated against the device clock. Every v1 shop and its customers are in the same timezone (IST), so this shows up only for a traveller reading a shop's open/closed state from another zone. A stored business timezone is a v1.1 change to the hours model. Deferred to v1.1 under decision D17 (owner to confirm).
The 'Block a specific date or time' row is hidden unless the viewer has the appointments scope, so a team member without it is no longer sent to a screen the guard bounces them from.
grep '#fff' in WeeklyHoursEditor.tsx: none (2026-09-16).
Shop-login has a screen: src/screens/business/BusinessLogin.tsx calls businessAccessService.login, and BusinessAccess exposes suggestLogin/setLogin ('Approve each sign-in').
BusinessAccess lists PENDING sessions and decides them (businessAccessService.decide, approve or deny). E2E critical/team-access drives a grant and a revoke.
Opening the editor on a FULL grant starts empty and says what's being given up, and saving refuses an empty scope list — the code comment explains why every scope ticked is not the same as FULL.
grant_team_member_access writes team-typed notifications, not QUEUE_UPDATE (production source check, 2026-09-16).
expiryLabel renders the session's expiry on each grant row (the comment records that it used to be fetched and never shown).
Revoking opens a confirmation (confirmRevoke), with the comment noting there is no undo — re-granting creates a new session.
